title: DNS over QUIC RFC 9250 0-RTT Replay Protection Architecture
purpose: Define DNS opcode classification for replayability, client-side 0-RTT gating, and server-side 0-RTT transaction handling when a hosting layer supplies early-data state.
design_summary: Three independent layers: (1) DoqDefaults.IsReplayableOpcode classifies DNS opcodes 0 (QUERY) and 4 (NOTIFY) as replayable and all others as non-replayable. (2) DoqClient exposes AllowZeroRtt; when enabled, QueryAsync rejects non-replayable opcodes with a clear exception. (3) DoqServerOptions.ZeroRttStreamDetector supplies the early-data signal to DoqQueryContext.IsZeroRtt; when true, non-replayable 0-RTT transactions receive a REFUSED response with Extended DNS Error "Too Early" before handler dispatch.
data_and_state_considerations: The client adds a boolean AllowZeroRtt flag. The server adds a nullable ZeroRttStreamDetector delegate; when it is absent, streams remain handshake-confirmed by default.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The transport layer does not currently expose 0-RTT detection on the server side; DoqQueryContext.IsZeroRtt defaults to false unless DoqServerOptions.ZeroRttStreamDetector supplies a true signal.
OPCODE values beyond the registered range are treated as non-replayable.
REFUSED response with EDE Too Early (option code 20) is constructed inline.
risks: The 0-RTT detection abstraction point is DoqServerOptions.ZeroRttStreamDetector; the default remains false until a hosting layer or future transport integration supplies early-data state.

supplemental_sections.heading: Transport Limitation
supplemental_sections.content: The repository's QuicConnection.ConnectAsync public entry point does not expose 0-RTT state. DoqServerOptions.ZeroRttStreamDetector is the adapter seam for hosts or future transport integration to supply whether an inbound stream arrived in 0-RTT data; when absent, streams are treated as handshake-confirmed.
